subject: Dispatcher: auto-wire single-attempt judge after each impl task
description: Make the per-task pre-merge code-review gate fire reliably. Today self-learn-judge is triggered purely by the DAG (a judge task J blocked_by its attempts goes ready when they finish, then the loop spawns it like any task) — but nothing forces a judge task to actually run the judge skill (it is prompt/handoff convention only), and single-attempt impl tasks get no judge at all. Update the dispatcher conventions (CLAUDE.md 'background-subagent dispatch' section + parallel-orchestrate / orch-loop skills as needed) so that when a substantive impl task is dispatched, the dispatcher ALSO creates a judge task wired blocked_by that impl task, skill-tagged to run self-learn-judge in single-attempt review mode, BEFORE merge. Gate on complexity/scope so trivial one-liners skip it (matches the conditional-boundary instinct). The judge task becomes ready when the impl completes and the loop spawns it — reusing the existing DAG-gate trigger, no new trigger machinery. Ensure the handoff envelope for the judge task carries enough to select the judge skill. Depends on the judge skill supporting single-attempt review.

summary: Added the "dispatcher pairs a single-attempt judge task" convention (no code, prose only). CLAUDE.md: new paragraph in the "Default to background-subagent dispatch" section, right after the "Wiring is the dispatcher's duty" para — dispatcher creates a judge task wired blocking (blocked_by) the impl task BEFORE dispatching, so it goes ready via the existing DAG-gate trigger when the impl completes (no new machinery); the judge prompt skill-tags self-learn-judge in single-attempt review mode against the impl attempt branch (code-review rubric → APPROVE hold-merge / KICK BACK, NEVER force-merge per the conflict-abort note); trivial one-liner/doc/config edits skip it via the existing triviality carve-out. skills/parallel-orchestrate/SKILL.md: matching one-bullet addition under step 3's serialize bullet. skills/orch-loop/SKILL.md left unchanged — it is the trigger CONSUMER (already documents judge-blocked-by-attempts going ready) not the impl dispatcher, so it already coheres. Committed d10ec59 on orch/attempt/f1653e44-5863-4644-bebc-963582c76510-3.
